spectral.true_color: Dark to medium greens dominate, interrupted by olive-gray and tan openings (high confidence). The top-center opening is particularly pale; a few smaller whitish flecks occur centrally and toward the right (high confidence). Dark belts have diffuse margins and retain a vegetated appearance (medium confidence).
spectral.false_color: Red occupies most of the patch, ranging from vivid red to dark crimson or burgundy (high confidence). Many pale true-color openings become gray-green or muted reddish gray, while surrounding vegetation remains distinctly red (high confidence). The darkest true-color belts retain red responses in several places (high confidence).

implications.claim: Widespread red responses support extensive leafy vegetation with appreciable near-infrared reflectance.
Variation in red intensity likely reflects a mixture of vegetation density, foliage properties and illumination; it does not independently establish vegetation health.
Pale tan areas with weak red responses probably contain more exposed soil or rock and less leafy cover than their surroundings.
Dark belts are more consistent with shaded or dense vegetation than with clearly identifiable open water.
Differences in soil or canopy moisture cannot be isolated confidently from these displayed colors.
No confidently identifiable water surface is available for assessing turbidity.
Small bright patches do not provide sufficient spectral or geometric evidence to identify buildings or other built surfaces.

spectral.not_revealed: These renderings do not establish species, crop identity, canopy height, biomass, soil moisture, water quality, substrate composition or disturbance timing (high confidence). Display scaling prevents quantitative reflectance or vegetation-index measurement from color alone (high confidence).

interpretation.claim: The patch is predominantly wooded, with a connected vegetation matrix surrounding irregular openings.

interpretation.evidence: Levels 2–4; top_center, middle_center and middle_right: pale lobed patches with weaker red responses, but no diagnostic management geometry.

interpretation.evidence: Levels 2 and 3; all cells: no clear crop rows, regular parcel system or irrigation structures; only one observation is available.

uncertainties: Cover fractions are visual estimates rather than a pixel classification; uncertainty is approximately several to ten percentage points per major class (medium confidence).
At 10 m resolution, individual trees, narrow tracks, small channels and most isolated structures cannot be reliably separated (high confidence).
Upsampling enlarges the display without adding ground detail; small flecks and apparent curves may reflect mixed pixels and interpolation (high confidence).
Dense shrubland, woodland and forest cannot be consistently distinguished from these renderings (high confidence).
Sparse vegetation, dry vegetation, exposed soil and rock overlap spectrally in the pale patches (high confidence).
Terrain shadow and canopy differences are confounded in the dark belts; their physical origin remains uncertain (high confidence).
No obvious cloud cover is visible, but subtle haze and illumination effects cannot be quantified (medium confidence).
Feature sizes describe approximate visible extents; fragmented complexes do not have uniquely defined boundaries or component counts (high confidence).
No clear roads, rivers, lakes or buildings are resolved; small examples may still be present (medium confidence).
Season, management history and active change cannot be inferred reliably from a single undated image pair (high confidence).

summaries.w25: Probably wooded terrain contains irregular sparse or exposed openings (medium confidence). Widespread red indicates leafy vegetation (high confidence); season and management remain unresolved.
summaries.w50: The patch is probably dominated by woody vegetation, with irregular pale openings concentrated toward the upper center and middle right (medium confidence). Extensive false-color red supports leafy cover (high confidence). Dark diagonal belts may reflect terrain and canopy variation (medium confidence). Season, management and climate remain unresolved.
summaries.w100: The 1.2 km patch probably contains about 65% dense woody cover, 28% sparse vegetation mixed with ground, and 7% exposed soil or rock (medium confidence). Irregular openings are strongest in the upper center and central to eastern cells (high confidence). Dark southwest–northeast belts may reflect canopy and terrain illumination (medium confidence). Extensive false-color red confirms substantial leafy vegetation, while pale openings have weaker responses (high confidence). No settlement or large water body is confidently identified. Crop identity, forestry activity, season, moisture and climate cannot be established from these renderings (high confidence).
summaries.w200:
This 1.2 km scene is probably a wooded landscape with irregular openings and uneven terrain (medium confidence). Visual cover estimates are 65% dense woody vegetation, 28% sparse vegetation mixed with exposed ground, and 7% predominantly bare soil or rock (medium confidence).

The strongest pale clearing complex occupies the upper center, with curved margins and vegetated islands (high confidence). Additional fragmented openings cross the middle center and middle right. Lower and western cells retain more continuous vegetation (medium confidence). Several dark belts trend approximately southwest–northeast; canopy differences and terrain illumination are plausible explanations (medium confidence).

True color is dominated by greens with tan and gray openings. False color shows extensive red vegetation and weaker red responses over pale ground (high confidence). This supports differences in leafy cover, but does not independently measure health or moisture (high confidence).

No clear settlement, large water body or regular crop-field system is identified (high confidence). Natural sparse ground and managed clearings remain difficult to distinguish (low confidence). Season, crop type, forestry history, active erosion, flooding and specific biome or climate remain unresolved. Ten-meter pixels and display interpolation limit identification of small structures, tracks and channels (high confidence).
summaries.w400:
The paired renderings show a predominantly vegetated 1.2 km landscape with connected woody-looking cover and irregular openings (medium confidence). Approximate visual fractions are 65% dense woody vegetation, 28% sparse vegetation mixed with exposed ground, and 7% predominantly bare soil or rock (medium confidence). These are broad estimates, not measured classifications.

The upper-center cell contains the most conspicuous pale complex, roughly 250–350 m wide and 300–400 m long, with lobed margins and vegetated internal islands (medium confidence). The middle center contains another broad opening, while the middle right has elongated, fragmented pale patches (high confidence). Western and lower cells generally retain more continuous cover, punctuated by small openings (medium confidence). Boundaries are mostly irregular or diffuse, and there is no clear rectangular field network (high confidence).

Dark belts cross the western and lower portions approximately southwest–northeast (medium confidence). Their appearance is consistent with dense or shaded vegetation, potentially influenced by relief, although elevation and drainage cannot be established directly (medium confidence). Narrow pale segments and isolated bright flecks cannot be identified confidently as roads or buildings (high confidence).

True color is predominantly dark to medium green, with tan and olive-gray openings. False color shows extensive vivid red through dark crimson vegetation, whereas many pale openings become gray-green or muted reddish gray (high confidence). This supports substantial leafy cover and spatial differences in vegetation density (high confidence). Red brightness alone does not establish physiological health, and moisture cannot be isolated from illumination and cover effects (high confidence). No confidently recognized water surface permits a turbidity assessment.

Natural sparse ground, exposed substrate and managed clearings are plausible explanations for the openings, but their relative contributions remain uncertain (low confidence). Forestry, crop rotation, irrigation, harvest, recent clearing, erosion and flooding cannot be confirmed (high confidence). No settlement cluster or large water body is confidently resolved. A wooded terrestrial setting is supported, but season, specific biome and climate are undetermined (high confidence).

At 10 m resolution, mixed pixels obscure small structures, individual trees, narrow tracks and channels. Upsampling adds no ground detail, and display colors do not support quantitative reflectance measurements. Temporal imagery and additional measurements would be required to establish change, management history or ecological condition (high confidence).
